column1: # Known bugs of upstream versions, for scripts/interop.sh.
# Entries exist for versions that are built as candidates (make
# candidate-stepfunc), so that one upstream bug is reported as such instead of
# hiding whether everything else works, and for a pinned version only when the
# bug cannot be avoided by an adapter and the behaviour it breaks is covered
# by another check (docs/COMPATIBILITY.md says which).
# Columns, separated by tabs:
#   1  adapter, or adapter:server / adapter:client for a bug of one role
#   2  upstream version, as print-capabilities reports it
#   3  extended regular expression matched against the operation and its flags,
#      or against the description scripts/interop.sh gives a value check
#   4  what is wrong (docs/COMPATIBILITY.md has the details)
#   5  the fixture of the runs it applies to (scripts/interop.sh FIXTURE);
#      absent: baseline
# For a pairing that involves the adapter at that version, a matching case
# may fail and is counted as "known bug" rather than as a failure. If no
# matching case fails any more, the run fails: the entry is stale and the pin
# can move.
